# KubeCell

> KubeCell gives every developer their own isolated Kubernetes cluster (VirtualCluster) on shared physical hosts. A single management cluster holds desired state; each Cell host runs the workloads. Developers get a standard kubectl-compatible K3s API with hard CPU/memory/GPU quotas, persistent storage, and kubeconfigs published automatically.

Status: pre-release (kubecell.io/v1alpha1). Not production ready.

## Key facts

- Four public CRDs under kubecell.io/v1alpha1: Cell, VirtualNodeClass, VirtualClusterPlan, VirtualCluster.
- Manifests stay small: you choose a host and a quota tier; versions, ports, and security defaults are handled for you.
- The management controller writes OCM ManifestWork objects and reads hosts only through the OCM cluster proxy.
- Each child cluster has exactly one logical node named `kubelet`; scale by switching quota tiers, not by adding nodes.
- Isolation: per-child host namespace with ResourceQuota, LimitRange, NetworkPolicy, and admission rejection of privileged/host access and hostPath volumes.
- Pinned stack: host K3s v1.36.3+k3s1, K3k v1.2.0, child K3s v1.34.2+k3s1, OCM Hub v1.3.1, TopoLVM on hosts.
- Built on upstream components (K3s, K3k, TopoLVM, OCM) through their public APIs; no custom scheduler, CNI, CSI, or device allocator.
